messages:
incident-bot: PAGED (P0) cont-batch latency spike >1.5s in us-east-1 — alert cb-latency-cliff. 90p token latency 2.4s, error rate up 1.7%. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/cont-batch-latency
oncall-anna: ACK. I'm on shift, investigating. Any customer pages?
cs-lead: support: 3 customers opened tickets for timeouts, one Dedicated account impacted, requesting ETA.
ryan-sre: Observing KV cache eviction rate +4x since ~00:13 UTC, microbatch backlog climbing. 12/48 inference nodes CPU ~90%. Logs show repeated "kv_cache_eviction=true" and "prefetch_overrun".
maria-sre: Hypothesis: high concurrency + aggressive merge heuristics in continuous-batching => microbatch collapse -> prefetch storm -> KV churn. Sequence lengths look normal.
sam-eng: I'll toggle PREFETCH to conservative and cap microbatch size as hotfix canary. Preparing commands now.
oncall-anna: Post the steps/commands so we can audit.
sam-eng: Snippet: ```kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cb-controller PREFETCH_MODE=conservative MAX_MICROBATCH=32
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/cb-controller --selector=region=us-east-1```
deploy-bot: Started rollout for deploy/cb-controller -> revision v2026.03. Canary pods: cb-controller-5, cb-controller-6.
maria-sre: Also adding admission throttle to dampen sudden spike: `/svc/adm throttle set --path /generate --rate 80rps --burst 40`.
ryan-sre: Canary results: eviction rate down ~60% on canary pods, 90p latency dropped to ~0.6s, backlog draining. +observability: kv_cache_eviction_count trending down.
cs-lead: Customers seeing improvement? Support notes one customer still getting intermittent 504s.
oncall-anna: Understood. Triage: keep canary roll and monitor 5xx threshold (rollback if >0.5%).
sam-eng: Rolling to all us-east-1 replicas now. ETA ~4m.
deploy-bot: Rollout progress: 30% -> 70% -> 100% complete. All us-east-1 replicas now at revision v2026.03.
ryan-sre: After full roll: global 5xx returned to baseline, CPU normalized, KV thrash reduced. Cache growth stabilized (slower).
pm-jess: Need quick customer impact summary for PG. Any SLA breaches?
oncall-anna: Preliminary: 3 customers reported degraded experience between 00:12-00:28 UTC. One Dedicated customer had ~2 minutes of tail latency above SLA. No data loss or exfiltration. Postmortem scheduled.
maria-sre: Root-cause hypothesis: a batching heuristic change increased merge aggressiveness under high concurrency -> microbatches shrank -> prefetch requests outran KV cache -> eviction storm -> disk IO and queueing -> jitter + 5xx.
sam-eng: Hotfix = conservative prefetch + MAX_MICROBATCH cap + admission throttle. Also added guard to prevent negative batch-size inflation. PR #5421 merged and deployed.
ryan-sre: Action items: 1) If similar spike in 24h, revert heuristic back to previous behavior. 2) Add kv_eviction_per_min metric and alert. 3) Enforce minimum canary traffic weight (>0.5%) when changing batching heuristics.
oncall-anna: Handoff: I'm handing to @maria-sre for next hour. I'm off in ~10m. Handoff notes pinned: https://redwood/incidents/INC-2026-2147/hand-off
maria-sre: ACK taking over. I'll watch for regressions. Escalation criteria: 5xx >0.5% OR node CPU >85% -> page infra. @cs-lead please update customers that mitigation is applied and we're monitoring.
cs-lead: Will update: "We've deployed a targeted mitigation and are monitoring system metrics. Expect next update in 30m".
deploy-bot: Incident mitigation applied, metrics improving. Recommend 2h continued monitoring before closing. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-2147.
incident-bot: On-call handoff recorded. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Goodbye."
